intended_object: The reverse of a dart in a simple graph: a dart (u, v) is an ordered pair of adjacent vertices, and its reverse is (v, u), which is a dart because adjacency is symmetric. Inferred from the docstring and the name.
explanation: The definition swaps the two vertices of the dart's underlying pair (`d.toProd.swap`). It proves the result is still a dart with `d.adj.symm`, i.e. from the symmetry of adjacency. That is exactly the standard reversed dart. The construction applies to any simple graph on any vertex type, so it is at its natural generality. No separate general Mathlib declaration of this object exists to cite; this definition is itself in Mathlib, in `Mathlib/Combinatorics/SimpleGraph/Dart.lean`.
